findings.issue_text: [High/bug] GroupAdapter.java:271 — The null guard is applied to only one of the methods that lazily resolve the backing model: the sibling getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (~line 269) and other getGroupModel() delegation sites (e.g. update() for mutations) still dereference the supplier result unchecked, so the same concurrent-deletion NPE remains reachable (e.g. via paginated sub-group listing). The null handling should be centralized in getGroupModel() or every delegation site guarded.

[Medium/api] GroupAdapter.java:274 — Returning null silently changes the contract of getSubGroupsCount(): callers that unbox or assume non-null (e.g. 'long count = group.getSubGroupsCount()') will now NPE at a distance, and REST payloads can surface subGroupCount: null to clients that previously always received a number. A defined outcome (not-found exception, or falling back to the cached sub-group list size) would be safer than null.

[Medium/data] GroupAdapter.java:274-275 — When the backing model is gone (group concurrently deleted), the fix serves a 'ghost' group with a null count instead of evicting/invalidating the stale cache entry, so a deleted group can keep appearing in listings with corrupted data until invalidation catches up. The cached entity should be invalidated when modelSupplier.get() returns null.

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java:140-158 — The reader thread is never joined: assertThat(caughtExceptions, ...) can execute while the thread is still mid-request, so an exception can be recorded after the assertion (false pass), and the thread can outlive the test method. Set the flag, join() the thread, then assert.

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java:153-156 — deletedAll is only set after the entire delete loop; if any remove() throws, the flag is never set and the non-daemon reader thread busy-loops against the server indefinitely, degrading the rest of the suite. Wrap the deletion phase in try/finally and use a bounded wait (latch/timeout).

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java:120-158 — The test provides no evidence that the race window was actually exercised (a read overlapping a deletion), so it can pass without ever hitting the fixed code path — including on an unfixed build — and it asserts nothing about eventual consistency (e.g. deleted groups eventually absent from listings). Add a signal that reads overlapped the deletion phase and verify final state.

[Low/performance] GroupTest.java:141-149 — The reader loop issues unthrottled groups(0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) requests in a tight loop with no sleep or iteration cap: it hammers the server/DB during CI, and any transient client-side error (timeout, reset) is captured as a failure, making the test slow and flaky.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows only `GroupAdapter#getSubGroupsCount()` was changed to bypass `getGroupModel()` and add a null check on `modelSupplier.get()`. No similar change is shown for the nearby `getSubGroupsStream(...)` method (mentioned by the finding but not included) or other delegation sites, so the fix is visibly localized/inconsistent. However, the claim that other methods *still* dereference a null supplier and that an NPE remains reachable cannot be directly verified from the provided hunks because `getGroupModel()` and the sibling methods’ implementations are not shown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` now does `GroupModel model = modelSupplier.get(); return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();` instead of calling `getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()` (which would likely throw if the backing model is gone). The finding’s core point—that when `modelSupplier.get()` returns null the adapter does not evict/mark the cached entry invalid—is accurate and grounded in this change. However, the claim that this will make a deleted group keep appearing in listings cannot be verified from the diff alone (no listing/invalidation flow is shown). It’s a concrete edge-case/behavioral concern introduced by returning `null` instead of failing/invalidating, but not provably a defect from the diff by itself.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupTest#createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a non-daemon thread is started that busy-loops calling `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` until `deletedAll` becomes true. However, `deletedAll.set(true)` is only executed after the entire delete loop completes, and the delete loop is not wrapped in `try/finally`. If any `remove()` call throws (or the test otherwise aborts before reaching `deletedAll.set(true)`), the flag is never set and the reader thread can continue running indefinitely (and it is not joined or marked daemon), potentially hanging/degrading the rest of the test suite. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java:120-158 — The test provides no evidence that the race window was actually exercised (a read overlapping a deletion), so it can pass without ever hitting the fixed code path — including on an unfixed build — and it asserts nothing about eventual consistency (e.g. deleted groups eventually absent from listings). Add a signal that reads overlapped the deletion phase and verify final state.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupTest#createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the reader thread is started but there is no synchronization to ensure it actually runs concurrently with the deletion loop (no latch/barrier, no join, no check that at least one read happened during deletions). The only assertion is that caughtExceptions is empty, and there is also no final-state verification that the deleted groups are absent from group listings. Therefore the test can pass without exercising the intended race window or validating the post-delete outcome, making it a concrete, diff-grounded test weakness rather than a product bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] GroupTest.java:141-149 — The reader loop issues unthrottled groups(0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) requests in a tight loop with no sleep or iteration cap: it hammers the server/DB during CI, and any transient client-side error (timeout, reset) is captured as a failure, making the test slow and flaky.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()` starts a background thread that continuously calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true);` in a `while (!deletedAll.get())` loop with no sleep/backoff or iteration cap. This is directly shown in the diff and can hammer the server/DB during CI and increase flakiness by treating any transient exception as a test failure (`caughtExceptions.add(e)` then `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`). It’s a concrete test/performance reliability issue introduced by this change, not a product correctness bug.
